clue.text: They might be, pressed to make reports

definitions.text: They might be, pressed to make reports

parts.words: They might be, pressed to make reports
parts.note: reads like documents squeezed out of officials, but the things pressed are on guns, and the reports are the bangs of shots

explanation.surface: Civil servants are leaned on until they produce their reports.
explanation.definitionFit: On a gun you squeeze a small lever to fire, and the firing makes a loud report, the old word for a bang.

clue.text: By putting up a possible catch, gets censure

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting a word up means writing it from bottom to top

parts.note: per means by, as in per post
a roach is a freshwater fish an angler might catch

explanation.surface: Someone is criticised for setting up a dubious door latch.
explanation.definitionFit: Reproach and censure are synonyms: both mean an expression of disapproval.

clue.text: Cricketer takes. Peter Pan character for a heroine .

parts.note: W. G. Grace, the great Victorian English cricketer
Wendy Darling and her brothers in J. M. Barrie's play

explanation.surface: A cricketer takes on a role from Peter Pan in a heroic part.
explanation.walkthrough: Grace Darling, a lighthouse keeper's daughter, rowed out in 1838 to rescue shipwreck survivors off Northumberland.
explanation.definitionFit: She became a Victorian national celebrity for her bravery in a sea rescue, the model of a brave woman.

clue.text: Time to see flat and arrange for lift

parts.note: even means level, flat
the sea's tide is what raises boats off the mud, lifting them on the flood

explanation.surface: Time to view an apartment and book the elevator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' is not a home but the adjective level; the tide is the sea's rise that lifts ships.
explanation.definitionFit: Eventide is a poetic word for evening, a time of day.

clue.text: Jack's supporter ?

parts.note: the Jack is not a man's name but the climber of a ..., whose tall church spire carries him

explanation.surface: Who backs Jack?
explanation.definitionFit: A steeplejack climbs church spires and tall chimneys, so the tall tower is what holds him up.

clue.text: Fish is 'not upset about wartime organization

indicators.note: the reversed word goes around the organization's initials
in a down clue, an upset word is turned over so it reads upward

parts.note: the word not is used as fodder
ARP, Air Raid Precautions, the British civil defence body of the Second World War

explanation.surface: A fish refuses to be bothered about the Home Front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns the printed word round, giving TON, and 'about' has that wrap the initials of Air Raid Precautions, the British civil defence service of the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: The tarpon is a large silvery game fish of warm Atlantic waters.

clue.text: Horse needs loading

parts.note: a young male horse that also shares its name with the revolver maker, and a gun must be loaded

explanation.surface: A packhorse is waiting for its burden.
explanation.definitionFit: A young male horse has the same name as the American revolver, which needs bullets put in before firing.

clue.text: Set out after recent floods

indicators.note: the shuffled letters come after the synonym for recent

parts.note: fresh means new, recent

indicators.note: set out suggests setting off, but out signals the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: Someone sets off after the latest floods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set out' reads as departing, but 'out' is the anagram signal, making ETS, and 'after' places it behind the word for recent.
explanation.definitionFit: A freshet is a sudden rise of a river from rain or melting snow, a flood.

clue.text: Opening of greyhound racing ?

parts.note: sounds like the start of a race meeting, but means the hinged gate at the front of a dog's starting box, called a trap

explanation.surface: A new greyhound stadium opens its gates for the first race.
explanation.definitionFit: Greyhounds start from boxes called traps, so the hinged flap that opens each one is literally a door of a trap, as well as the everyday hinged floor hatch.

clue.text: Some' Shanghai passengers returning from a Samoan port ?.

indicators.note: the run found in the words is then read from right to left, coming back on itself
only some of the letters of the words that follow are used, a run tucked across them

explanation.surface: Travellers who were press-ganged in China are on their way home from a South Sea harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' picks AIPA out of shanghAI PAssengers; 'returning' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Samoa is a harbour town on the island of Upolu.

clue.text: Looks at story script about a S. American river

parts.note: a conte is a short tale, the French word used in English

indicators.note: the letters for script go around the river's name

parts.note: MS is short for manuscript, a handwritten script
the River Plate is the estuary between Argentina and Uruguay

explanation.surface: Someone reads a screenplay set on a South American river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'script' is the abbreviation for manuscript, and 'about' splits it so the river sits between its two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To look at something long and thoughtfully is to ponder or gaze at it, a synonym.

clue.text: Fagin's helper led fort guard astray

indicators.note: going astray means wandering off course, so these letters stray into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone led a fort's sentries off in the wrong direction.
explanation.definitionFit: In Dickens's Oliver Twist the pickpocket Jack Dawkins, nicknamed this, works for the thief-master Fagin.

clue.text: Indian leader called scholars to 'carry hat

annotationWithheld.why: 'Indian leader called scholars to carry hat (6)': GANDHI fits 'Indian leader', but no reading of 'called scholars to carry hat' builds the letters, and a search of the clue gives no parse.
annotationWithheld.clue: Indian leader called scholars to 'carry hat

clue.text: A sort of floor-covering well known to pressmen'?

definitions.meaning: a type of linoleum, read as lino plus type
the hot-metal line-casting machine familiar to newspaper printers

explanation.surface: A kind of lino that every printer recognises.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as LINO TYPE, it is a kind of floor covering; whole, it is the line-casting typesetting machine used by newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: The first reads lino type as a variety of linoleum; the second is the hot-metal typesetter that cast whole lines for newspaper printers.

clue.text: Commands attacks ?

definitions.meaning: orders, instructs someone to do something
rushes at, makes an onslaught, as cavalry do

explanation.surface: Orders and assaults.
explanation.definitionFit: To charge is both to give someone a duty or instruction and to rush forward in assault.

clue.text: Fish place-on canal where there's weed

parts.note: the char is a trout-like fish of cold lakes
a lock is the gated chamber that raises boats on a canal

explanation.surface: A fish finds a spot on the canal where weeds grow.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlock is wild mustard, a yellow-flowered weed of arable fields.

clue.text: Attempts to run through fencing perhaps

definitions.meaning: pushes or tries, as in the thrust of an argument
the stabbing lunges a swordsman makes to pierce an opponent

explanation.surface: Efforts to dash through a garden fence.
explanation.definitionFit: A push or try is a forceful effort; in swordplay the same word is the lunge meant to pierce an opponent.

clue.text: Could be a' jolly 21 holiday ?

parts.note: points to the entry at 21 for the kind of holiday, a short mid-term break

explanation.surface: Perhaps a fun break from lessons.
explanation.definitionFit: British pupils have a short break in the middle of each term, a week off between the long holidays.

clue.text: Man gets the same rise-disturbed -Roe.

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means reading from bottom to top

parts.note: do, short for ditto, means the same again

indicators.note: disturbed letters are knocked out of their order

parts.note: the word roe used as fodder

explanation.surface: A man ends up with the same sort of fish eggs, stirred up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rise' turns DO into OD; 'disturbed' makes ROE into ORE.
explanation.definitionFit: Theodore is a man's first name, so it can stand for a male person.

clue.text: Smashing type of cask

definitions.meaning: someone or something that breaks things
a small water barrel carried in a ship's boat

explanation.surface: A violent sort of barrel.
explanation.definitionFit: One who smashes things is a destroyer; the same word is a sailor's term for a small keg of drinking water.

clue.text: Indian city, gives a civilian, title to one Russian ruler

parts.note: Mr is the title given to a man with no military or noble rank
I is the Roman numeral for one
a tsar was the emperor of Russia

explanation.surface: An Indian city grants a plain Mister to a former Russian emperor.
explanation.definitionFit: This Punjab city is home to the Golden Temple of the Sikhs.

clue.text: Wild lochs contain nothing but a lot of fish

indicators.note: the shuffled letters hold the letter for nothing
wild letters run free into a new order

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Untamed Scottish lakes hold nothing but shoals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' makes SCHOL from LOCHS; 'contain' puts O inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A large group of fish swimming together is a shoal, for which this is a collective noun.

clue.text: Account book 'tackled by anglers?'

definitions.meaning: a kind of fishing rig in which the bait lies on the bottom, held by a weight

explanation.surface: Fishermen grapple with the accounts.
explanation.definitionFit: A bookkeeper's main record book shares its name with the bottom-fishing rig that anglers use, hence 'tackled'.

clue.text: Generous 'settlement, Thrale agreed

indicators.note: a settlement arranges matters anew, so these letters are settled into another order

explanation.surface: Mr Thrale, Dr Johnson's friend, consents to a lavish financial settlement.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry Thrale was a brewer and friend of Samuel Johnson; 'settlement' rearranges THRALE AGREED.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone open-handed and kind has a big heart, so this compound means magnanimous.

clue.text: Horse ran round the ring

indicators.note: the word ran goes round the circle letter

parts.note: O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A horse galloped about the arena.
explanation.definitionFit: A roan is a horse whose coat is mixed with white hairs.

clue.text: Stupid-fellow appears to -make progress.

explanation.surface: A dim man looks as though he is getting somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: A goon is slang for a fool; split in two it is the phrase for proceeding or carrying on.

clue.text: Many, increase egg output. with this weapon

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a crossword stand-in for many
hens that increase output lay more eggs

explanation.surface: A poultry farmer is urged to boost egg production with an unlikely tool.
explanation.walkthrough: A claymore is the large two-handed Scottish broadsword.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish broadsword is an example of a bladed weapon.

clue.text: There's money in the plant, it's said'

indicators.note: the money word is placed inside the plant's name

parts.note: a reed is a tall waterside grass
the mark was the German currency

explanation.surface: Gossip has it that cash is hidden in a pot plant.
explanation.definitionFit: To remark is to comment or observe aloud, so the past tense is a synonym of spoke or stated.
